articles.title: CommerzVentures launches €50M Fund IV targeting early-stage AI and fintech startups
Frankfurt-based CommerzVentures closes €50 million Fund IV, betting on early-stage FinTech and AI

brief.essentiel: CommerzVentures , a Frankfurt-based specialist venture capital firm focused on financial services, has closed its fourth fund at €50 million.
points: The fourth fund — CommerzVentures IV (Fund IV) — is anchored by Commerzbank and is deliberately smaller than its predecessors; the firm managed over €550 million across three prior funds, including €300 million in Fund III .
“ Fund IV is deliberately smaller because we want to invest earlier.
We aim to combine early conviction with the experience, industry connections and hands-on support founders need to build their businesses ,” said Judith Vogel , Partner, CommerzVentures.
Founded in 2014, CommerzVentures is a specialist financial services investor having backed more than 40 companies across its three previous funds.

articles.title: Playbook raises €8M to help pharma companies keep AI agents compliant
German startup Playbook secures €8 million to help pharma companies deploy AI safely

brief.essentiel: Munich’s Playbook , a startup developing neurological AI to ensure rule-based compliance in pharmaceutical industries, has raised €8 million to turn documents into data AI can read, but not change.
points: In Germany, Munich-based Interloom raised €14.2 million for AI-agent knowledge infrastructure, Berlin-based Cognee secured €7.5 million for AI memory technology, and Stuttgart-based Blockbrain attracted €17.5 million for secure enterprise AI agents.

Elsewhere, London-based Pharosyn raised €2.5 million for pharmaceutical intelligence software, while Barcelona’s Mafer AI secured €2 million for AI-enabled R&D and regulatory workflows, and Barcelona and San Francisco-based Modern Relay raised €2.5 million for enterprise AI infrastructure.
Source: EU-Startups EU-Startups previously covered lead investor Heal Capital’s participation in Swiss startup CGC Genomics’ €1.7 million round , supporting regulated AI applications in oncology.
Together, these rounds represent approximately €46.2 million in 2026 funding, rising to €54.2 million including Playbook’s new investment.

articles.title: Bcomp secures €20 million from EIB to scale flax fibre-based alternatives to carbon fibre, glass fibre and plastics

brief.essentiel: Bcomp , a Fribourg-based CleanTech startup specialising in high-performance bio-based materials, has secured €20 million from the European Investment Bank (EIB) to build a high-volume manufacturing plant in the Romanian city of Timișoara and continue research and development in Fribourg.
points: This EIB backing takes the form of €20 million in venture debt, supporting the company’s €47.6 million investment programme to expand manufacturing capacity in Romania and further develop its R&D activities in Switzerland.
“Europe needs to turn technological innovation into industrial production if we are to strengthen our competitiveness and accelerate the green transition.

By supporting Bcomp in Romania and Switzerland, we are helping European innovation reach industrial scale and unlock new opportunities for sustainable growth,” said EIB Vice-President Ioannis Tsakiris .
Founded in 2011 by Christian Fischer and Julien Rion, Bcomp develops composite materials based primarily on flax fibres instead of conventional carbon fibre, glass fibre and plastics.

articles.title: UK active business numbers back above 2019 level after three-year fall

brief.essentiel: The number of active businesses in the UK has reached 2,889,575, back above its 2019 level after falling in 2022, 2023 and 2024, according to The UK Business Health Map .
points: The UK Business Health Map is a new interactive resource created by 365 Finance.

The SME lender has analysed the Office for National Statistics’ data on business demography, business openings and closures covering the past decade, including the latest data released on 19 November 2026.

In visualising vast data sets, the resource provides insight into the health of the UK’s private sector, including how many businesses are opening and closing in different parts of the country, and how this varies by industry.
The map will be updated each time ONS publishes new figures, providing entrepreneurs and leaders with up-to-date information to help in decisions about where to start and scale their businesses.

articles.title: OPINION: AI will favour the companies built for AI, not adapted to it

brief.essentiel: For decades, business leaders have been warned that the impending arrival of a new technology will completely reorder the corporate world.
points: But for the best part of the last thirty years, it did not.
With AI, however, the warning deserves more consideration.
The web, mobile phones, cloud computing and social media, for example, were all predicted as disruptors that would sweep the incumbents aside.
The reason is less to do with the technology itself, but rather who is best placed to use it, and that is increasingly becoming startups, rather than established companies.

articles.title: Adyen’s co-founder Pieter van der Does to retire as Co-CEO; Ingo Uytdehaage to become sole CEO

brief.essentiel: Pieter van der Does, co-founder and Co-CEO of Dutch Fintech Adyen , is stepping down from his executive role after 20 years at the helm of one of Europe’s most prominent technology companies.
points: In an announcement on 23 November 2026, marking Adyen’s 20th anniversary, the company said van der Does will retire on 31 December 2026, and Ingo Uytdehaage, Co-CEO since 2023, will become sole CEO “ After 20 years, this is the right moment for me to step down on a positive note and with a very good feeling.
Ingo and I have worked very closely together as Co-CEOs, and now we have completed the transition ,” said van der Does , co-founder and co-CEO of Adyen.
During Q3 2026, the company reported net revenue of €738.1 million, a 23% year-on-year increase, while processed volume climbed 30% year-on-year to €451.1 billion.
Adyen has been my life’s work, and I’m incredibly proud of what our teams and customers have built together over the past two decades.

articles.title: Is Silicon Valley turning its back on Europe? Plug and Play’s Thomas Bigagli weighs in

brief.essentiel: Sequoia Capital’s decision to close its London office has reignited debate about the future of European innovation and the commitment of US investors to the continent – especially amid other departures including Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue.
points: However, not all US investors in Europe share this gloomy outlook.

articles.title: OPINION: Europe’s rearmament risks creating empty factories

brief.essentiel: Weapons factories are springing up all over Europe as proof, many say, that the continent is taking its rearmament seriously.
points: Build factories, manufacture arms and kit, and Europe, faced with aggression on its eastern flank and the changing realities of a complex, multipolar world, will be able to take care of itself and its interests after decades of low defence investment.
Because supply chains, the networks of production and distribution on which all manufacturing relies, are not all in Europe, and do not scale in proportion to manufacturing.

To think that they do is to believe, wrongly, that a company may get funding, massively improve its production capacity, and never have to worry that a chip, or some unusual component, might stop it from manufacturing anything.

Indeed, weapons factories are expanding at three times the rate they did in peacetime, covering some 7 million square metres of new industrial development, but whether Europe is pursuing the right industrial policy.
